Mr. SPEAKER informed the house that the deputy of His Excellency the Governor General had been pleased to give in His Majesty's name the royal assent to the following bill:
An act for granting to His Majesty certain sums of money for the public service for the financial year ending the 31st March, 1931.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE

speechtext: The house resumed consideration of the motion of Mr. Mackenzie King for committee of supply and the amendment thereto of Mr. Heaps.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, when the interruption occurred we had a good representation on the treasury benches. That representation
is at the present time somewhat depleted, but there are one or two ministers remaining.
I want to draw to their attention some of the difficulties which obtain due to recent enactments. The Minister of Justice is in the chamber-

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: The Minister of Justice is always in the chamber.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: When the bell rings for the next election you will have a little more syrup to hand out to your constituents.

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: Maple syrup?

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
There will be a little more cream left for you; they will not allow it to go to the country to the south, a country which economically is penetrating Canada to such an extent as has never before been known. Not only has that country penetrated Canada from an economic standpoint, but it is throwing out ideas which are being absorbed by our younger generation through reading American magazines and books. What is the government doing about it? The government is doing nothing to stop this economic penetration; it is doing nothing to stop the adoption of American ideals in this country. It is allowing the United States to send in vast quantities of products manufactured by them, products even of their farms and market gardens.
When the interruption occurred I was proceeding to read from the columns of the Manitoba Free Press. I quote:
All that a government can do is to create a set of subsidiary conditions which permit the people to take advantage of their opportunities to the fullest extent possible. There will be no argument that Mr. King and his government have done so.
Of course there is no argument that they have done so. They have not only failed to create such a set of conditions as the Free Press declares it to be their duty to create, but they have brought about and encouraged an opposite set of conditions under which foreign capital is enabled to exploit Canadian resources with foreign labour in foreign countries, and then to exploit the Canadian market with foreign manufactures. From such a source as the Manitoba Free Press, the rebuke may be judged the most severe one which has been administered to Mr. King and his cabinet.
The unemployed are not among those who lost heavily in the stock market crash; they are not among those suffering from the wheat blockade. Those who lost in the stock market were able to buy their Rembrandts, their radios and their Turkish rugs. It is such men

Unemployment-Mr. Heenan
as the 1,132 who were lined up at the soup kitchens in Montreal the other day who are interested in unemployment. They are our kith and kin who demand the opportunity to be gainfully employed in order that they may be able to sustain their families.
We must have for this country a policy which will provide work for the minds and hands of all kinds and classes. Such a policy will never be forthcoming under the maladministration we have witnessed during the last eight years-take another drink, Mr. Minister of Labour-with ministers almost denying their leader, one minister in one direction, another in another; with ministers who will not act when they have the opportunity. In my opinion it has not been a fair "shake " for the workingmen of this country.
In conclusion I ask this government to face the issue fairly and squarely when the time comes, and not try to turn it up some side alley.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, I am not going to
attempt to follow the last speaker, because I was not aware that we were in the throes of an election; I did not know we were preparing for an election at the present time. At any rate, I am glad to know that the hon. member reads the Manitoba Free Press and believes in some of the ideas expressed therein. I hope he will always follow, believe in and quote from the Free Press, especially during the next and every other election.
I thought we were discussing the amendment to the motion to go into supply, which was moved by the hon. member for North Winnipeg (Mr. Heaps), and I desire to congratulate the hon. member for bringing up this very important matter on the floor of the house. I have no doubt that the purpose of the amendment was to enable a discussion to take place with regard to this very important question of unemployment, and great credit is due the hon. member for the moderate language which he used, which indicates his sincerity of purpose in bringing this matter to the attention of the house.
During the course of his speech the hon. member for North Winnipeg asked, among other things, that something should be done immediately for the unemployed. I might state that the purpose of the motion to go into supply was to secure funds with which to carry on public undertakings and let further contracts which would aid the unem-ploj'ed.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: The Prime Minister said the estimates of the Department of External Affairs were to be considered.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: We have just granted two months' supply, so you can go right ahead.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Another matter strongly
advocated by the hon. member for North Winnipeg was unemployment insurance, and in that connection he quoted from my remarks as contained in the London Advertiser of March 15 and asked me to explain my position. I desire to take this opportunity of making my position clear, if it is not clear already. First let me say to hon. members who are advocating unemployment insurance that their appeal is no stronger than the appeals I made on the floor of the Ontario legislature when I was a member of that house. I thought at that time, and still think, that that was the proper place to advocate a contributory unemployment insurance plan.
When the hon. member for North Winnipeg brought this matter before the house a couple of sessions ago and asked that it be referred to the committee on industrial and international relations, no objection was raised by any member on either side of the house. That committee met and worked diligently in connection with this matter, and a report was brought in directing the government to refer the question to the provinces. Last session again the hon. member brought in a similar resolution asking that the question be referred back to the same committee. That was done, and after a good deal of hard work the committee arrived at certain conclusions which they brought before the house in their final report. They endorsed the principle of a compulsory contributory plan of unemployment insurance, but stated in effect that they had received the views of the law officers of the crown, which were that it was a provincial matter. The recommendations made by that committee were brought before parliament, and parliament adopted the report. It is true that an amendment was offered by the hon. member for North Winnipeg which, if it had been adopted, would have asked the provinces to pass legislation giving up their rights in this respect. That amendment was defeated by a very large majority.
The report also recommended that the government, at the next Dominion-provincial conference, place this matter on the agenda and bring it before those attending the conference. This government did not wait for such a conference to be called; as soon as the report was printed it was sent to the provinces in order to ascertain their views. I think everyone will agree that it is far better for the provinces to have time to consider such an important matter as the adoption of

Unemployment-Mr. Heenan
an unemployment insurance scheme before discussing it at any conference.
Unemployment insurance will be adopted in Canada only after public opinion has been educated to the necessity for such legislation. The unemployment insurance scheme in effect in Great Britain has been so very much misrepresented in Canada that our people have not yet a true understanding of what unemployment insurance really means, or of the system which is in vogue in England. It has come to be represented in this country merely as a dole. Then again, some newspapers in this country have taken the position that there is no use discussing the question of unemployment insurance in Canada until it is known what system is in the minds of those who advocate it. Personally I am very much interested in some definite, permanent plan which will give something to our unemployed so that they will not need to look for relief every winter or during every season of unemployment. I took occasion at London to tell of a plan which I had in mind, in order to stir up public discussion and help form public opinion.
In this case public opinion certainly must include the working men, because if the working men are to be compelled to contribute part of their wages to any such scheme, of necessity they must know what is in view and what they will be expected to do. I know a number of working men-and I have known more since I made my remarks at London- who oppose a contributory system of unemployment insurance. Many claim that the employer should stand the whole cost, so that in a country like Canada it is necessary first to form public opinion along these lines. In view of that, and in view of the fact that this parliament has spoken already in regard to this matter, my remarks can apply only in the light of what parliament already has said. Parliament has not said that the federal government should contribute to any plan of unemployment insurance. My statement at London, and I thank the hon. member for North Winnipeg for reading from the Advertiser, because I have myself referred him to that paper-was very plain in that regard. I claimed that a simple method could be worked out which would apply to the railroad men much more readily than to the men in any other industry, and I said:
A system could be inaugurated in this country which would be suitable to Canadian needs. Take, for example, our Canadian railroad workers-in the summer time there are upwards of 200,000 men employed, and during the winter periods there are about 25,000 of those workers laid off for several months. The wages of all railwaymen average about $130
per month. If a fund were created, it would take about $5,000,000 to pay these employees half-pay for three months,
I had not in mind a plan which would operate for twelve months of the year, but rather one which would apply to the winter season. My remarks at London continue:
-say January, February and March; the employees contributing about one per cent of their wages and the railway companies the balance. This would not be too hard on either, and, if necessary, the governments could assist.
In the light of what has occurred in this parliament, and in the light of the opinions given by the law officers of the crown, I could not mean anything else but the provincial governments. I went on to say that this system could be extended to every line of industry.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: That is a very sharp corner.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Some hon. members on
the other side of the house know what sharp corners are.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: We see the minister running around them.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Even if it is a sharp
corner, it is better to go around it than to say nothing at all. I am not afraid.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Especially when you can
back up afterwards.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
My remarks continue:
This system could be extended to workers in every industry and would provide a permanent system.
I agree with my hon. friend from North Winnipeg that the workers are entitled to a permanent system. I then said that the House of Commons had endorsed such a system. My hon. friends will notice that I did not confine myself to saying the Liberals had endorsed this system, but I included my hon. friends in that endorsation. I then stated:
Parliament has also declared it is a provincial matter, and the government has taken the matter up with the provinces, but notwithstanding the fact that it is a provincial obligation, the Prime Minister has stated that if the provinces so desire his government is prepared to cooperate with them in establishing a uniform system.
I could not go beyond the limits set by my leader, who, on February 27, in answer to a question from the member for Winnipeg North Centre said:
My recollection is that a special committee of this house considered this question last session and brought to the house a report to

Unemployment-Mr. Heenan
the effect that unemployment insurance was necessarily a matter with which provincial governments rather than the federal government would have to deal. I think I expressed the view yesterday that in my opinion a system of unemployment insurance would be a constructive way to deal with the unemployment problem, to which system not only the employer and the governments concerned would contribute but the worker also. If the provinces make a move in this matter and it appears that the federal government can be of assistance in helping to bring about uniformity as between the provinces of any plan proposed, or can cooperate in other ways in any discussion on the subject, we shall be glad upon invitation to take the matter under consideration.
During the course of my remarks at London I said that I would do my utmost in this regard, and I propose to stand by that statement. So long as I remain in public life I intend to work to the end of providing a solution to this unemployment problem. It may be that I become too enthusiastic about these things. I remember after the Old Age Pensions Act was passed that I went through this country from coast to coast speaking to members of the different provincial governments and upon different platforms in an effort to arouse enthusiasm for this measure in the provinces. Many letters came to members of the government and several editorials were written asking the Prime Minister to keep his Minister of Labour at home where he could mind his own business. My hon. friends across the house prophesied that the Old Age Pensions Act would not benefit any one man or woman in Canada because no province would desire to participate in the plan. They were mistaken in their forecast because I am glad to state that about 35,000 old men and women of this country are receiving benefits through the provisions of that act.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: How many?

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: I think it is about 35,000, although I may be one or two thousand out.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: How many provinces are participating?

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: The majority of the provinces, and three more are now considering the matter.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I am glad you follow the
lead given by the hon. member for Winnipeg North Centre.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
This amendment asks that the government should take immediate steps to deal with unemployment. The government is asking for supply in order to start the construction of public works. The question has

been asked, what is the government doing to relieve unemployment? I remember when my hon. friends across the way were in power one principle enunciated by them was that work should be given and not relief. We propose to give as much work as possible to take care of the unemployed. We are doing something now, and all last winter we put on a large program of public works, much of which might have been postponed until a more favourable season.' We urged the railroad companies to go ahead with their program of extensions and their orders for supplies, equipment, et cetera, and I think it is generally acknowledged) throughout the country that the Canadian National went ahead with a good deal of work that might very well have been deferred until a more favourable season.
We have also contributed something in our immigration policy. Contrary to what my hon. friend across the floor would say, by order in council we prohibited employers of this country from going over to European countries and bringing in contract labour.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Has that not been the
law for many years?

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: No.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I am pretty sure it has.
You cannot bring anyone into this country by contract.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: They were brought in by the thousands when my hon. friends across the floor were in power.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I think the minister is
astray.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: They are bringing them in to-day, but we do not catch them all. Only recently we had to consider the question of letting a contract to build a ferry in this country. The government could have had that ferry built in Great Britain for about one-half the cost that we are going to expend on it in Canada. In order to give employment to Canadian workers we will expend far more than a million dollars extra on that particular work. We are now putting into operation the eight-hour day for government employees. We are also, with the consent of hon. friends opposite, putting into operation the eight-hour day in connection with all public works and public contracts.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: Could the minister give the house the actual cost of labour involved in constructing that ferry?

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
The contract is away over $2,000,000. There is also the fact that during

Unemployment-Mr. Heenan
last winter we contributed in the neighbourhood of $600,000 for unemployment relief for war veterans. I am not saying we should not have done that; I am just telling the house some of the things we have done. Hon. members will realize that the passage of the War Veterans' Allowance Act will also contribute a considerable amount next winter towards the relief of unemployment.
I notice that the hon. member for North Winnipeg (Mr. Heaps) was very moderate in his language; there was not a semblance of politics in his whole speech. But such was not the case with hon. members who spoke from the Conservative side, and I did not expect it would be, because one realizes there are very few questions, whether it be mothers' allowances, workmen's compensation or any other humanitarian piece of legislation, out of which they will not endeavour to make political capital. They have discussed the question of federal responsibility; they have talked about unemployment and its causes, the tariff, immigration, and so forth, and have stated that the Dominion government should have contributed something towards the excess cost in the municipalities. It might be well to review the history of unemployment relief measures in this country. During the years following the war, when unemployment was prevalent throughout Canada, there was a cry for financial assistance not only from one or two provinces, but from every municipality and every province, and the federal government rendered financial aid. The policy of the government at that time was declared through the Minister of Labour in a letter dated the 14th of December, 1920. It was addressed to the Hon. Walter Rollo, Minister of Labour in the Ontario government, and in this letter I find the following statement:
The situation should be met to the utmost possible extent by the provision of work instead of the provision of relief.
He stated further on in the letter:
I feel sure the .provincial and municipal authorities will join in to provide a substantial amount of employment and in this way the situation should be materially relieved.
A little further on he said:
Every possible effort should be made to avoid the necessity of any other form of relief.
And in another part of the letter we find this statement:
Should, however, the emergency relief measures become necessary by reason of utterly unavoidable shortage of employment, the federal government is willing to cooperate.
And he outlines a system of cooperation of paying one-third of the excess cost over normal
construction. But all the way through his letter he emphasizes local, municipal responsibility. Everyone knows that the system which was put into vogue at that time was neither equitable nor satisfactory; because hon. members will readily understand that when there is an offer of excess cost over normal construction, it is only the provinces that have large construction work to do and only the municipalities that are financially strong enough to put on a program of construction work, that can take advantage of this. Therefore, the majority of the provinces or of the municipalities did not participate in any such scheme.
The hon. member for Fort William (Mr. Manion) will possibly be making a speech in the house on this subject, but I notice that in Winnipeg he made a speech in which he took exception to my statement that unemployment was primarily a municipal responsibility and, secondly, a provincial responsibility.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: If these matters of importance to labour be provincial responsibilities, what is the use of the position which the minister now holds? How can he justify to the workingmen of Canada the $14,000 paid to the minister if he cannot do anything?

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
My hon. friend knows it
would embarrass me to tell of all the good works the Minister of Labour does, so that if he is really desirous of ascertaining what the value of this position is, I would advise him to ask the labour men of Canada, the men who urged the establishment of the Labour department of this government.
I was saying that the hon. member for Fort William took exception to my remarks, at least as reported in the press. I could not understand his objection when I read it because I recall that the hon. member for Fort William was a member of the cabinet in 1921. and on October 7 of that year, some time after he had been sworn in, an order in council was passed dealing with this important question, from which I quote this paragraph:
Unemployment relief always has been, and must necessarily continue to be, primarily a municipal responsibility, and in the second instance the responsibility of the province.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: If the minister will permit me, did not the government of the day contribute one-third of the cost to assist the provinces in the relief of unemployment?

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I think my hon. friend
from Vancouver Centre (Mr. Stevens) was also a member of the cabinet at that time.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
And we contributed.

Unemployment-Mr. Heenan

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I was giving my hon. friend the enunciation of their own policy as it appears in the order in council. I will read it again so that there may be no misunderstanding:
Unemployment relief always has been, and must necessarily continue to be, primarily a municipal responsibility, and in the second instance the responsibility of the province.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: May I ask that this document be read in full, Mr. Speaker? It is a public document, and when public documents of that character are quoted we are entitled to have the full text.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: I intend to read it. I would like to read it over and over again, because I get inspiration from it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: You need it badly.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: If I have made any mistake at all, it is where I have been following in the footsteps of my hon. friends opposite.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: You have followed nearly everybody else's footsteps in the country at different times.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: Sometimes I catch up to them.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
We are entitled to have
this document read.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: I will read it in a minute or two. It is good reading.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: The minister has already stated that he intends to read the order in council.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: Before I read it, I want to say to my hon. friend from Vancouver Centre and to the hon. member for Fort William, who, as reported in the press, assailed the government in Winnipeg and said that unemployment relief was a federal responsibility-

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
May I just correct my
hon. friend? I said that it was a joint responsibility of the municipalities, the provinces, and the Dominion. I have right here the clipping from the press. That is the same statement that I have made on different occasions, and I adhere to it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I think at this juncture,
I had better read the order in council, because it is an interesting document. It is P.C. 3831, dated October 7, 1921, and reads:
The committee of the privy council have had before them a report, dated 5th October, 1921, from the Minister of labour, submitting that the problem of unemployment, and means best calculated to relieve it, has been receiving 
constant study and attention since about De-. cenxber, 1920. On December 14, 1920, a federal relief policy was announced, the object of which was to aid responsible municipal authorities to fairly meet existing needs and prevent suffering to any citizen *nulling to work but unable to obtain employment. It provided for payment by the federal government to any municipality of one-third of the amount disbursed by the municipal authorities for unemployment relief-

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: That is an inspiration for you.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: There will be a few more inspirations before we get through.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: That is an inspiration this government needs, too.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
It is good reading. I will repeat that sentence:
It provided for payment by the federal government to any municipality of one-third of the amount disbursed by the municipal authorities for unemployment relief, together with a proposal that provincial governments join in on an equal basis. The federal government's disbursements for this purpose since January, 1921, have been over $600,000. Many gratifying expressions of appreciation have been received, in most cases accompanied by the suggestion that employment should be provided instead of paying unemployment doles. Since July 13th the Department of Labour has been in communication with provincial governments, mayors of municipalities and others as to improved methods of dealing with the situation next winter.
It was suggested to the provincial governments that, inasmuch as the extent of unemployment, as well as possible remedies, varied in different provinces, a provincial survey by conference or otherwise might he made by each provincial government, after which a conference of provincial representatives might meet with the federal government to discuss the problem and devise some general plan of assistance to the municipalities, upon whom the duty and responsibility of dealing with relief primarily rests.
Three provincial governments only have thus far signified concurrence in the suggestion for a central conference of provincial representatives, two of which desire the representation to extend to organizations other than governmental.
I would ask my hon. friends who are clamouring for a conference to listen to the next sentence:
Inasmuch as a federal conference with wide basis of representation would be both cumbersome and expensive, of doubtful value, and, thus far, only approved of by three of the provincial governments, and, further, because of the necessity of early decision and action, if useful service is to be rendered, the minister recommends that the following federal policy of basic principles on unemployment be approved.
1.	Unemployment relief always has been, and must necessarily continue to be, primarily a municipal responsibility, and in the second instance the responsibility of the province.

Unemployment-Mr. Heenan
2.	That because of the present situation being due to causes beyond the power of local, or even national control, provincial and federal governments should cooperate with municipal authorities
So the situation had got beyond local control, beyond provincial control, beyond even national control. Before I get through I will examine the present situation to see if it i3 as bad as the situation prevailing in 1921.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: Much worse.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
It continues:
in,
(a)	helping to create and provide employment.
(b)	where employment cannot be furnished to workmen who are willing to work, to aid in providing food and shelter for themselves and dependents until the present emergency period is past.
3.	That federal funds used for unemployment relief or for relief work must be disbiirsed only through responsible municipal authorities, who in each case shall bear at least one-third of the total or extra cost.
The minister further recommends that the federal government agree to participate in the cost of work provided by municipalities to relieve unemployment on the following basis:
(a)	Municipalities to bear the normal cost, that is to say, the cost of carrying on the said work in the normal working season.
(b)	Estimate of normal cost to be approved by federal government's engineers in the Department of Public Works.
(c)	That municipal, provincial and federal governments bear equally and jointly the actual cost over the estimated normal cost, thereby encouraging the creation of employment where possible.
(d)	That where work cannot be provided the federal government continue to refund one-third of tiie disbursements actually made by a municipality for unemployment relief, conditional upon the provinces participating on an equal basis.
Then:
The committee concur in the foregoing recommendations and submit the same for approval.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: AVhy did you not copy that yourself?

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: I will explain that before I get through.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: That is a real inspiration.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: If my hon. friends will only possess their souls in patience for a little while I will tell them why I did not do it. I wonder why the member for Fort William takes me to task so seriously for imitating what the government of which he was a member initiated at that time.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: Not at all. We absolutely offered to help in every way, and did help; but you refused.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: They said that it was first a municipal and then a provincial obligation pure and simple. I wonder why, for instance, they did not take Premier Ferguson to task?

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: Because Premier Ferguson helped in many ways. I was with the deputation from northern Ontario that interviewed him. He assisted us. He did not put us off with the hot air that we get here.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: The hon. member for Fort William did not come down here.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: Yes, I was on the deputation and listened to the Prime Minister's remarks, which he says now mean nothing.

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: Order.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: Order yourself.

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: You have already made three speeches.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: You often make too many yourself.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Let me quote what appeared in a press despatch of January 24, 1928:
Hopes for unemployment relief from the provincial government were blasted at the meeting of the York township council yesterday. A letter written by Premier Ferguson, in answer to an appeal sent from a recent session of the council, made it plain that the province was not prepared to take any such action. Premier Ferguson stated in his letter "that unemployment is an entirely municipal affair". "It would not be just," he said, "to use the money contributed by the whole province for purely local relief. The municipality derived the benefits from the working men in times of prosperity and should be prepared to bear the burden when times were not so bright." He added, "The only time when the province had rendered any such assistance was just following the war."
I have heard my hon. friend take the premier of Ontario to task for that statement. I think probably the public would expect the Dominion government to take more notice of the representatives of the provinces with respect to their requirements than of gentlemen who are not elected to represent the provinces. In this connection I should like to remind my hon. friends-

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Do not members of the
House of Commons represent their respective provinces?

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I did not mean it just in that way. I think the public of Canada would expect the federal government to take more notice of the representations of the provincial premiers as to the requirements of the prov-

Unemployment-Mr. Heenan
inees than 'they would even of the members in the federal house who are not elected for provincial matters.
Since all these things took place we have had a Dominion-provincial conference in Ottawa, and the question of the Dominion contributing unemployment relief was on the agenda for discussion. I should like to read from the blue book the result of that conference.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: What date is that, 1927?

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Yes.
The question of unemployment relief was but briefly dealt with. With the possible exception of Manitoba, no speaker urged federal aid in this direction. Several of the representatives in fact were of the opinion that unemployment relief on any fixed basis was simply an encouragement to unemployment. The representative from Manitoba, however, cited the case of Winnipeg, where at times by reason of itiner-a.nts wandering in unemployment was frequent, though labour conditions were fairly uniform. He believed that if the Dominion government did not undertake to bear any share in the cost of looking after these strangers, it should establish a depot for the relief of those who drifted m from the outside.
That is a pronouncement on this question by the premiers of the provinces.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: That is three years old.

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: That is not very old.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: Yes, we are all getting older.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Unemployment is increasing. Mr. LAPOINTE: The principle is the same.
_ Mr. HEENAN: I find again this year-this is not three years old-that Premier Ferguson made another statement. On January 24, 1930, he had this to say.
Our unemployment problem is spotty in various sections of the province; it centres chiefly in Toronto; but we are paying the one-third excess cost to municipalities, which seems to be meeting the situation.
There was no complaint from the provincial authorities of Ontario that they were not meeting the situation, but simply a bald statement that they were contributing one-third, and it was meeting the situation. I have not heard my hon. friend from Fort William say anything about that.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: I repeat, Mr. Speaker, that the premier of the province assisted northern Ontario when we came down and asked for help. I was on the deputation and know what I am talking about.

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: Repeat that later on.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Neither have I heard my hon. friend nor any of his colleagues say anything with respect to the statement made by Premier Tolmie of British Columbia. In a despatch dated Victoria, February 6, 1930, he is reported as follows:
.1 am not in a position to say anything about the unemployment situation here.
He added:
The responsibility of caring for destitute people rested primarily with the municipalities.
That is the opinion expressed by the premier of British Columbia.
Now, Mr. Speaker, I have been criticized in some quarters for not calling a national conference-

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: You are repeating what you said before.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: I beg your pardon?

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
The minister just stated
that at the Dominion-provincial conference Manitoba was the only province which did not accept responsibility for unemployment. I think he knows quite well that Alberta refused to accept full responsibility, and was of the opinion that the federal government as well had some responsibility in the matter.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I did not say anything
about the position taken by any of the provinces; I read from the reports of the proceedings of that meeting, and so far as I am concerned it speaks for itself.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
But the Minister of
Labour has in his possession a statement made by the premier of Alberta, which I sent to him only a few weeks ago.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Yes, and the premier of
Alberta has this report also.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: What was the last statement on this question made to the minister by the premier of Alberta?

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I forget what it was but it was not in accordance with this report. I happened to be present at the conference also, you must remember.
I have been criticized by some hon. gentlemen opposite for not calling a national conference, which to me is a very serious question. I feel that to call a national conference during a season when unemployment prevails is not going to help that unemployment very much. I can imagine municipalities and provinces, which might have work in contemplation or actually undertaken, holding up that work for a while and coming to Ottawa to find

Unemployment-Mr. Heenan
out who was to pay for it. Our Conservative friends, in their order in council, stated that such a national conference would be at any rate of doubtful value.
Hon. gentlemen want me to follow the example set by the United States; in fact it has been stated on the floor of the house that the government could very well emulate what President Hoover has done. I want hon. gentlemen to know that so long as I am in public life I propose to do what I think is best for the working men of Canada, whether or not it follows what has been done in the United States. I wonder if hon. gentlemen realize that when that conference was called at Washington and the unemployment and distress were shown, one of the first things asked of the labour representatives was whether they would promise not to ask for an increase in wages or for better conditions. I want to say that before I would take the responsibility of calling a conference to do that to the workingmen of Canada, I would want to know that I had the majority of those working men behind me. H you have followed what has been going on in the United States you will know that the conference has not had the result claimed by some of my hon. friends. I thought I knew whether or not I was doing what the majority of the labour men of this country wanted me to do when I did not recommend to my colleagues the calling of a national conference, and I was glad to know, as I am sure my hon. friends will be, that when the Trades and Labour Congress of Canada representing the majority of the workers of this country, met here, our action in not calling such a conference was endorsed.
I am not going to follow the system advocated by my hon. friends with respect to unemployment when they were in power. I well remember reading in Hansard of one hon. member who stated in 1921 that the cause of unemployment was that industries were becoming insolvent and therefore could not give work, and it was stated that the reason they were becoming insolvent was because the working men would not give a fair day's work. I remember those words very well, and I am sure every person in Canada who was interested in labour never will forget them.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: Who said that?

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I will give the name of the hon. gentleman and the page in Hansard after a while, so my hon. friend can read it for himself. I hope, however, that hon. gentlemen opposite will have changed their minds in that regard after having been out of office for such a long time. The same hon. member 2419-75
said that the only cure for unemployment would be to go through a period of depression such as the country was going through at that time. I am not going to adopt that position with regard to the unemployment situation.
When I was interrupted a short time ago I was going to say that some hon. members had misunderstood or misinterpreted my statement with regard to unemployment. It was made to appear by some of my hon. friends that I was unsympathetic and did not really realize that there was unemployment in this country. I want to point out that at the time I made my statement I was dealing with the request to call a national conference. During my statement I not only acknowledged that there %vas unemployment but advocated a means of alleviating that condition. I went on to point out that the federal government was undertaking a large program of public works and that we were asking the railway companies to do the same thing, and I stated that if the provinces and the municipalities would follow that example it would relieve unemployment to a certain extent. It is true that I quoted some statistics to show the amount of employment in this country as compared with that in the United States, but I am afraid those figures did not suit some of my hon. friends, because they adopted the slogan "statistics do not feed hungry stomachs." It appears to me that those figures were too strong for my hon. friends to stomach. The statistics are there; they were not gathered for that year particularly but have been gathered for many years past from the same sources. The statistics at that time, and up to February 1, showed a comparatively greater number employed in Canada than in the United States.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I should like to ask the
minister whether it affects Canadians or Americans when he speaks about unemployment in the United States. Is it a matter of chasing Canadians back home or is it a matter of putting Americans out of employment? Answer that.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I am not going into
statistics to-night, although I have them here if it is necessary.
The Prime Minister was criticized when he made his speech for saying that the country was in a prosperous condition, and for quoting from statements made by the heads of financial institutions. I am not going to quote from suich statements, but I am going to quote from the statements made by premiers of our provinces as to what condition those provinces were in at the end of 1929.



Unemployment-Mr. Heenan
Beginning at Prince Edward Island, this is what Premier Saunders had to say:
The island is, however, prosperous. Nineteen twenty-nine has been a successful year. In agriculture and its branches of stock raising and dairying, much progress has been made.
Then he goes on to say:
We look forward to the year 1930 with confidence and optimism. Our people, in common with Canadians generally, are conscious of the urge resulting from a sense of past achievements and .the promise of a great destiny in store for Canada.
Premier Rhodes of Nova Scotia made this significant statement:
There has been a distinct improvement in conditions surrounding our steel-coal industry and prospects for stabilized winter employment are most promising. Real progress has been made in the development of mines other than coal mines, notably at Stirling in Cape Breton, where the zinc lead deposit has about reached the point of regular production, and the further development of our gold mines.
In addition to that he has this to say: Taken as a whole the outlook for the coming year is distinctly bright. I am fully confident that marked as has been our progress during the past few years, there are even better things in store for this province. Our future is assured. The extent of our progress and prosperity depends largely upon the amount of individual effort which we are prepared to put forth.
Premier Baxter of New Brunswick states the following:
New Brunswick has enjoyed one of the most prosperous years our people have ever known, with agricultural and industrial activity especially marked, and a substantial upbuilding taking place in virtually every field of development.
He goes on to say:
The financial position of the province has been markedly improved this year by the successful culmination of negotiations which have been in progress for some time to have the Saint John Valley Railway taken over from the province by the federal government as a part of the Canadian National Railways system.
We will not refer to the statement made by Premier Taschereau. Still, I do not see why we should not read what that gentleman has to say about the province of Quebec:
In spite of many counteracting factors, general prosperity has prevailed throughout the province of Quebec during 1929. Much advance has been made in some of the most important domains, notably in agriculture.
We now come to the statement made by the Hon. G. Howard Ferguson, premier of the province of Ontario:
During the past year Ontario has maintained the steady progress that has long been characteristic- of this province. In all important departments there has been satisfactory advance, and in many ways the outlook for the future has been improved.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: What is the date of that, please?

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
The statements I have
been reading are dated January 14, 1930. To continue with the statement by Mr. Ferguson:
In the considered judgment of our financial experts, the position of Canada is fundamentally sound, and this is especially true of the province of Ontario.
Mr. Ferguson is speaking not only of the province of Ontario, but of Canada as a whole. He says:
We are constantly growing and expanding and our faith in the outlook is firmly established by experience.
Next we have the statement made by Premier John Bracken of the province of Manitoba:
It is a common belief that Manitoba is a purely agricultural province. It is true that agriculture is still her chief means of maintenance, but during recent years other industries have grown and prospered until to-day the annual value of their gross output closely rivals that of farm products. The year 1929 has seen substantial progress in this direction. During the past year thirty-six new manufacturing concerns have been established in Manitoba, while twenty-two others have extended their plants. It seems certain the total output will substantially exceed that of 1928, which was estimated at $159,252,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: Have you any quotation from the remarks of Mayor Webb of Winnipeg?

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: He is the mayor of the city, and not the premier of the province of Manitoba.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: But he is the man who is faced with the unemployment problem in the city of Winnipeg.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
We have next the statement made by Premier Anderson of Saskatchewan :
The settling of our vacant farm lands and the development of industries are reacting favourably upon the growth of our urban centres. The population of some of our larger cities has increased fifty per cent in the last three years. Since January 1st of this year the total value of building permits issued for construction work in the province amounted to $34,000,000. as compared with $20,000,000 for the year 1928.
The future progress of Saskatchewan rests upon the firm foundation of the productive effort of our people, aided by a discriminating immigration policy. Capital from eastern Canada and the British Isles is increasingly available for the development of our natural resources. The achievements of the past have been considerable. We have merely scratched the surface of our vast resources, however, and there is every indication that the future holds in store tremendous possibilities for the people of Saskatchewan.

Unemployment-Mr. Heenan
Premier J. E. Brownlee of the province of Alberta has the following to say:
At the end of another year the province of Alberta finds itself in a strong financial position. At the end of March, 1929, the fourth successive surplus was reported. The surpluses for the past four years have been as follows:
1925		$ 188,019 54
1926	 17,800 53
For the fifteen months ending March 31st:
1928		$	279,763 13
1929	 1,578,823 09
Further on in the article he says:
Therefore, we face the end of the year in a spirit of confident optimism, believing that the next few years, at least, will be years of continued development, both agriculturally and industrially.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: Would the minister intimate to the house what he is trying to prove?

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: I thought the hon. members would like to hear this.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: The .minister has scrupulously avoided stating what the mayors of Edmonton, Winnipeg, Vancouver, and other cities have said.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: The hon. member must realize that sometimes a man chooses to eat and drink what other people do not like.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Will the
minister quote the appeals made by Premier Brownlee and possibly some others to the government for relief?

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I shall be very glad to do that in a little while; I have those statements somewhere among my papers. I am trying to answer hon. members opposite who have criticized the Prime Minister because he has stated that Canada is prosperous. I am trying to show in my own humble way just what the premiers of each of the provinces have said. I know it is hard medicine to take, but my hon. friends sometimes prescribe for others and I would like them to take a little of their own medicine. Premier Tolmie of British Columbia has this to say:
British Columbia has just closed another active year in all its primary lines of industry. Completed returns should show that the forestry output for 1929 will surpass all previous records for quantity, though, owing to falling prices, values will be somewhat lowered.
Then he goes on:
With new mines discovered and old mines developing, with all our primary industries expanding, with additions contemplated or in progress in our abundant hydro-electric powers there appears at this time to be no good reason why 1930 should not be a banner year for British Columbia.
As an ordinary layman I have tried to figure out how Canada can be in such a deplorable condition as stated by my hon. friends when the premiers of the different provinces have stated that their own provinces are each prosperous.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: Are the minister and his colleagues aware of any unemployment problem which exists in Canada at the present time or which has existed during the past three months?

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: Certainly not.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: In my statement of December 16 I stated that the government had asked the railway companies to go on with their extensive programs of expansion, and I suggested that the provinces should do likewise. When the government of the province of Ontario was about to go on with the construction of the highway from the head of the lakes to the Manitoba boundary, which highway had been promised for years and years at every provincial and federal election,, and which had been started, the hon. member for Fort William went down with a delegation to consult with the provincial government. They returned home and stated that the province would go ahead with the work if the federal government would contribute 50 per cent of the cost.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: We did not say anything of the kind. Mr. Finlayson, the Minister of Lands and Forests, made a statement in writing that they would do that. The provincial government is ready to do its share but this government has not shown a readiness to do anything.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: That highway has been promised at every provincial and federal election. My hon. friend did not succeed in stopping the provincial government from going ahead, because an announcement has been made in the press that the work will be started when the snow is off the ground.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: Does the minister suggest that I tried to stop the provincial government from going ahead with that highway?

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
My hon. friend went down to Toronto and after consulting with the provincial government about the highway, the construction of which was an obligation upon the provincial government, he returned with the statement that the provincial government would go ahead with that which they were obligated to do if the federal government would contribute 50 per cent of the cost.

Unemployment-Mr. Heenan

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: They were not obligated to build a trans-Canada highway unless they wished.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Would the province of
Quebec be obligated to build a highway through the province of Ontario?

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: The whole house, with the possible exception of those under the command of the government whips, has asked that a trans-Canada highway be built.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: Which is the trans-Canada highway ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: A part of that highway is the highway about which the minister is trying to fake right now.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: How does the hon. member know this?

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: It is that part which the minister has refused to support but which has the support at the present time of his constituency.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: I have heard that a meeting of Conservatives from the north was held and the proposal was that if by any chance the Dominion government called this bluff and said that a contribution would be made towards that highway-

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
This government is not
[DOT]calling anybody's bluff.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: -the Conservatives up in Timiskaming district were to claim that the highway should go through their way instead of through Fort William and Kenora. I am satisfied to allow the electors in that part of the country to deal with this matter. The Conservatives are trying to find an excuse for the province of Ontario delaying the highway a few months longer.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: They dealt with that question at the last election and they beat everyone who was put up against them.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: I know one member they did not beat.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: The minister made a bet upon a public platform, which was a corrupt practice.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: The trouble with my hon. friend is that he knows I won the bet.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: I would like to know what the Prime Minister thinks of one of his ministers making a bet on a public platform.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: I just called one of my hon. friend's bluffs.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: The minister did not do any such thing. He made a bet on a public platform and his bluff was called.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: He called for relief money.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: It might be well to discuss unemployment for a little while.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: This highway was discussed upon the platform at Sioux Lookout and Kenora during the last provincial campaign. The vote taken in the House of Commons last session-and my vote is shown there-was shown to the people in that country, but notwithstanding the man who opposed the Conservative candidate was elected by a majority of over four hundred.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: What has that to do with unemployment?

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: I have shown that the premiers of each province have stated definitely that at the end of this year they were all in good financial standing. I have not heard any of those gentlemen complain that they are not able to cope with unemployment in their province, although the Prime Minister has left the door open.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: He surely has.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: They came down here to the conference of 1927 and stated that they did not wish any contribution towards unemployment relief, and that statement has not been reversed as yet.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: The minister should not make a blanket statement like that.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
The premier of Alberta
has asked for a contribution but has not stated that he cannot cope with this matter himself. He has said that that province has the greatest surplus in its history.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: That was before the unemployment began.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: They said in 1927 they did not want relief, and their statements I have read were all made at the end of the year 1929. The Premier of Alberta did not state he could not cope with this situation; instead he said that his province is in such financial condition that they have the greatest surplus in their history.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: As of March, 1929.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
January.

Unemployment-Mr. Heenan

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
No, 31st March, 1929, a
year ago.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: I do not propose to make any excuses in regard to unemployment. I am not going to stand here and say that I have the cure for it. I am not going to agree with my hon. friends who say that the way to cure unemployment is by protection. Neither am I going to agree with my hon. friends who have stated that because the federal government has charge of immigration, it is responsible for unemployment. I can recall the great clamour there has been for many years from that side of the house for a wider immigration policy. I can recall the hon. member for Vancouver North (Mr. McRae) advocating in the house a couple of sessions ago a policy whereby we should bring 250,000 or 300,000 families into this country. He advocated doubling the population of western Canada. Yet I find that the hon. member for Vancouver North a few weeks ago stating that the federal government, on aocount of bringing in so many immigrants, was responsible for unemployment. I think I can recall even a question on the floor of the house some time ago when the hon. member for Vancouver Centre was reported in several newspapers, when he went over to the old country, as having said that there was a job waiting in Canada for every unemployed miner in Great Britain if he was physically fit.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I never made any such
statement.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: I am glad to know there are others who can be misunderstood or mis-reported once in a while.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: It is misquoted.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I will read the hon. member's own statement. There is a question in Hansard of March 30, 1928, page 1854. The matter was brought u,p by the hon. member for Comox-Alberni (Mr. Neill). The hon. member for Vancouver Centre is reported in the Sunday Times of London, England, of December 4, 1927, as follows:
"Every unemployed miner in Great Britain," said Mr. H. H. Stevens, M.P., Vancouver, who arrived in Liverpool yesterday on the Canadian Pacific liner Melita. " can be found employment in the Canadian mines, provided he is physically fit."

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: Read a little more. That is not the statement.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
That is the statement
which appears in Hansard.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
It is a distorted extract
out of an interview which was given.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: I believe that, and I will not read any more. If the hon. member says he did not say that, I believe him, because I know no sensible Canadian would make such a statement.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I quite agree with the
minister. Then why the insinuation?

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Because that went into
thousands of homes of British miners of England who were looking for jobs, and no doubt thousands came to Canada because of that misstatement. On the one hand statements going out about "blue ruin" are driving Canadians out of the country, and on the other, statements about "wide spaces with a job for every man" are bringing them in. Is it any wonder we have unemployment in this country?

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: We have the admission.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: Hear, hear.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: It is no wonder we have unemployment. My hon. friends may applaud. It is no matter to laugh at that thousands of men who have come to this country through misrepresentations in the press or statements by hon. members, find that they cannot secure jobs here.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: That is utter nonsense.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: Before I leave the immigration policy, let me point out that the hon. member for Fort William said on the floor of the house, "Canada should be the mecca for the surplus people of the whole world."

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: So it should if we had a proper government and a good policy.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: Then my hon. friend goes to Winnipeg and says ithat we are bringing in too many immigrants.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I did not make any such statement in Winnipeg.
Mr.	HEENAN:	The hon.	member	is
reported as saying that.
Mr.	MANION:	I am not	reported	as
saying that. My hon. friend is just talking.
Mr.	HEENAN:	The hon.	member	forWillow Bunch (Mr.	Donnelly)	quoted from
his statement the other day and I will quote it to-morrow.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Nobody quoted it because I was never reported as saying any such thing.
Questions

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: My hon. friends blow hot and bfow cold for political expediency, nothing more and nothing less. Is it any wonder they find there are hundreds or thousands of men out of work? They say that all these things have been done by the federal government, lack of policy on tariffs, immigration and all these other things are responsible for unemployment; yet they have continually advocated immigration from the housetops.

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Has the hon. member
finished?

maintopic: SUPPLY-UNEMPLOYMENT AMENDMENT OF MB. HEAPS TO MOTION FOB COMMITTEE
speechtext: No.
